creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`matches()` returns a bool and there is no capture or find-all API. Three structurally different workarounds arose independently across the corpus:

- Write to a temp file and shell out to `rg -oe`: `jmx:98-111`, roughly 14 lines plus a subprocess plus an `rg` dependency, in a script averaging 6.4 seconds.
- Guarded `replace()` abuse with `$1`: `jira-title-sync.rad:21-24`, `argus:232-233`, `dklogs:29`. Silently returns the input on no-match.
- Peel one match per loop iteration: `tag-macro.rad:23-30`.

Sketch from the reports: `match(s, pat) -> {match, groups}|null` and `find_all(s, pat, *, group=0)`.

Already tracked on the main board as "regex text match function", in `high`. Larger than the `escape_regex()` card in p0-tier1, which is why it sits here.

---

### Orientation

- New builtins are docs-first: the `## Signature` line in `docs/funcs/<name>.md` **is** the type-checker's signature. There is no parallel definition in Go. Read `docs/funcs/README.md` for the full file contract before writing anything.
- The regex engine is already Go's `regexp` (RE2). `core/func_matches.go` compiles the user pattern directly, and `core/func_replace.go` already exposes capture groups through `$1` substitution - so capture extraction is new surface, not new machinery.
- Runtime dispatch and arg binding live in `core/funcs.go`: a `FUNC_X` name const plus a `BuiltInFunc{Name, Execute}` entry in the registration slice.

### Where to start

- `core/func_matches.go` is the closest template - it shows `f.GetStr("_str").Plain()`, `f.GetBool("partial")`, `f.ReturnErrf(rl.ErrInvalidRegex, ...)` and `f.Return(...)`. The `rl.ErrInvalidRegex` code already exists, so no new error code is needed for a bad pattern.
- `docs/funcs/matches.md` - signature `matches(_str: str, _pattern: str, *, partial: bool = false) -> bool|error`. Note `matches` anchors to the whole string by default (`"^(?:" + pattern + ")$"` in `core/func_matches.go`) and only matches substrings under `partial=true`. A capture/find-all API that anchored by default would be useless, so pick the opposite default and say so explicitly in the doc - the asymmetry with `matches` will surprise people otherwise.
- Returning a map: `NewRadMap()` plus `SetPrimitiveStr` - see `core/rad_time.go:12-33` and `core/func_parse_date.go` for a builtin that returns a structured map.
- Registration: `FUNC_MATCHES` is declared at `core/funcs.go:113` and registered at `core/funcs.go:336`. Follow that pair.
- Decide the null-vs-error shape for "no match" up front. Rad is errors-as-values; `docs-web/docs/guide/error-handling.md` is the current idiom reference. The card's sketch returns `null`, which reads better here than an error, since no-match is an ordinary outcome.

### How to verify

```sh
make generate                 # regenerates rts/signatures_gen.go, rts/embedded_funcs/,
                              # rts/embedded/functions.txt, docs-web/docs/reference/functions.md
make build                    # produces bin/radd (NOT rad - a bare `rad` is the installed release)
./bin/radd yourscript.rad
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=functions/match
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestDocSnippets
make test
```

The `=` in `-update=...` is required; a bare `-update -run X` swallows `-run` as the update value. Review the `.snap` diff afterwards.

### Done when

- `docs/funcs/<name>.md` exists for each new function, with a parsing signature, parameters, and at least one example. `core/testing/funcdocs_test.go` fails if the doc is missing, the signature does not parse, or it disagrees with the registered builtin.
- `make generate` output is committed - CI runs `make verify-generated` and fails on stale codegen.
- Snapshot cases under `core/testing/snapshots/functions/` cover: no match, one match, multiple matches, named vs numbered groups, a malformed pattern, and an empty-string match.
- `make test` is green.

### Watch out for

Go's RE2 has no backreferences or lookaround. Anyone reaching for capture extraction is likely coming from PCRE; the doc should say what is not supported rather than letting them discover it through a compile error.
title: Add regex capture extraction
